health-check.name: health-check
health-check.description: Internal health check. Verifies that the storage layer is accessible and ripgrep binary is available. Workspace role: ctx.volume (workspace volume via backend callbacks) rooted at /workspace. Admin role: native node:fs over the whole host (no callbacks involved).

list-roots.name: list-roots
list-roots.description: List the workspace roots this MCA can access. In the ctx.volume architecture, the root is always `/workspace` (the volume root) for the workspace role — the host root `/` for the admin role. Useful for auditing scope when a path is rejected by the sandbox.

read-file.name: read-file
read-file.description: Read a text file with optional line-based pagination. Returns content formatted as "cat -n" (numbered lines) plus metadata (name, size, lineCount, kind). Use offset+limit for ranges or head/tail for the first/last N lines. Returns text content; binary files are rejected.

params.head: Return only the first N lines (overrides offset/limit)
params.tail: Return only the last N lines (overrides offset/limit)
params.includeRaw: If true, include raw content (without line numbers) in addition to formatted

read-files.name: read-files
read-files.description: Read multiple text files in a single call. Returns an array with one entry per requested path (ok, content/error). Each file is read with the same default limits as `read-file`; pass perFileLimit to override. Failures on individual paths do not abort the batch.

read-binary.name: read-binary
read-binary.description: Read a binary file (image, PDF, audio, archive, …) and return base64 + detected MIME type. For text files use `read-file`. Hard cap 10 MB to avoid blowing up the chat context.

create-file.name: create-file
create-file.description: Write content to a file, overwriting if it exists. Safety: an existing file must have been read first in this session (use `read-file` before overwriting). For new files, parent directories are created automatically. Use `edit-file` for in-place modifications and `append-file` for additions.

append-file.name: append-file
append-file.description: Append content to the end of a file. Creates the file (and parents) if it does not exist. Does NOT require a prior read (appends are non-destructive to existing content). For replacing content, use `create-file` (after `read-file`) or `edit-file`.

edit-file.name: edit-file
edit-file.description: Replace exact string occurrence(s) in a file. By default fails if `oldString` appears zero or multiple times — pass `replaceAll: true` to rewrite every match. The replacement is literal (no regex). Returns a unified diff of the change. For structured hunks use `patch-file`; for larger rewrites use `create-file`.

params.filePath: Path to the file to edit
params.dryRun: Preview the change (returns diff without writing). Default false

patch-file.name: patch-file
patch-file.description: Apply a unified diff (patch format) to a file atomically. Useful for multi-hunk fixes where several edits must go together. Uses fuzzy matching (fuzzFactor 2) so minor context drift is tolerated. Returns whether all hunks applied. For single-point changes prefer `edit-file`.

params.filePath: Path to the target file to patch
params.dryRun: Preview the patch (returns diff without writing). Default false

list-files.name: list-files
list-files.description: List directory entries with metadata (name, type, size, mtime, kind). Optionally recursive via `depth`. Honors `ignore` patterns (glob-style) and `respectGitignore`. Paginates with `limit` + `cursor`. For a hierarchical view use `tree-view`; for pattern-based search use `find-files`.

params.path: Directory to list (default: `/workspace`, the volume root)
params.depth: Max recursion depth (0 = current dir only, default 0, max 20)
params.respectGitignore: If true, honor .gitignore from the volume root

tree-view.name: tree-view
tree-view.description: Return a hierarchical JSON tree of a directory up to `depth` levels. Files have size and mtime; directories have children. Honors `ignore` patterns and `respectGitignore`. Capped by maxNodes to prevent runaway output. Use `list-files` for flat pagination or `find-files` for pattern match.

file-info.name: file-info
file-info.description: Return metadata for a single path: exists, type (file/directory), size, mtime, permissions. Does NOT read content. Prefer this over `read-file` when you only need to check existence or size.

params.path: Path to the file or directory (e.g. '/workspace/docs')

hash-file.name: hash-file
hash-file.description: Compute the cryptographic hash of a file (default sha256). Reads the file via ctx.volume and hashes in memory. Useful for integrity checks and detecting changes between reads.

find-files.name: find-files
find-files.description: Find files matching a glob pattern (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}"). Results sorted by mtime (most recently modified first). Honors `ignore` patterns and `respectGitignore`. Use `search-in-files` for content search and `list-files` for flat directory listing.

search-in-files.name: search-in-files
search-in-files.description: Search file contents for a regex pattern using ripgrep. `output_mode` controls the shape: "content" returns {file, line, match, context} objects; "files" returns one entry per matching file with matchCount; "count" returns only totals. Supports context lines (-B/-A), include glob, case insensitive, multiline. Shell-injection safe (args are not interpolated). For finding files by name use `find-files`.

params.pattern: Regex pattern (Rust regex syntax via ripgrep)
params.path: Base directory or file (default: `/workspace`, the volume root)
params.contextBefore: Lines of context before each match
params.contextAfter: Lines of context after each match
params.type: Pre-defined file type filter passed to ripgrep --type (e.g. js, py, rust, ts, go, md). Faster than `include` when you target a known language
params.multiline: Allow pattern to match across newlines
params.limit: Max matches or files to return (default 50, max 100)

delete-file.name: delete-file
delete-file.description: Delete a file or directory. Set `recursive: true` for non-empty directories. Idempotent: succeeds silently if the path does not exist (reports existed=false).

params.path: Path to the file or directory to delete (e.g. '/workspace/old-dir')

copy-file.name: copy-file
copy-file.description: Copy a file or directory. For directories set `recursive: true`. Fails if the destination exists unless `overwrite: true`. Parent directories of the destination are created automatically.

params.source: Path to the source file or directory (e.g. '/workspace/docs')

move-file.name: move-file
move-file.description: Move or rename a file or directory. Fails if the destination exists unless `overwrite: true`. Parent directories of the destination are created automatically.

params.source: Path to the source file or directory

create-directory.name: create-directory
create-directory.description: Create a directory. By default creates parent directories as needed (recursive). Idempotent: returns created=false if the directory already exists.

params.path: Path to the directory to create (e.g. '/workspace/docs')

name: Filesystem
description: Filesystem operations within the workspace volume (/workspace paths): read-file (with batch), create-file, edit-file (exact-match + patch-file), navigate (list-files/tree-view/file-info), search (find-files/search-in-files with ripgrep + context), and manage files. Strict /workspace prefix (canonical form shared with mca.teros.bash), path-traversal safe, shell-injection safe, gitignore aware.

changelog.notes: Strict /workspace prefix: paths must start with /workspace (exact segment match) — anything else fails with a Forbidden hint so agents self-correct. Outputs now emit /workspace-prefixed paths so they round-trip with bash. find-files/search-in-files resolve the local root from MCA_VOLUME_MOUNT_PATH || MCA_WORKSPACE_PATH (fixes cross-workspace searches hitting the global /workspace symlink). Admin role support: MCA_FS_ROLE=admin switches to native node:fs over the whole host (dead code since mca.teros.admin.filesystem was retired on 2026-10-19 — pending removal).
Read, write, edit and patch files, browse folders, search by name or content, and manage media and hashes
